reformed.name: Reformed
reformed.definition: Salvation is God's work from first to last: he chooses whom he saves, calls them, and keeps them to the end (Calvinist; the Westminster, 1689 Baptist and Three Forms of Unity confessions).

heretical.name: Traditional heretical
heretical.definition: A teacher of the early church whom a council of the whole church later condemned by name, kept for his reading of the text: Origen (Constantinople, 553), Didymus the Blind and Evagrius Ponticus (680 and 787).

neutral.name: Neutral
neutral.definition: Argues no system: language, history, reference, or a creed every tradition confesses.

mixed.name: Per author
mixed.definition: A collection of many writers; each note carries its own writer's label.

entries.name: Matthew Henry's Commentary
entries.author: Matthew Henry
entries.description: Verse-by-verse devotional exposition of the whole Bible, finished after his death from his notes.

stance.label: reformed
stance.why: Presbyterian Nonconformist minister; Westminster theology throughout.

entries.name: Church Fathers by verse
entries.author: Many writers
entries.description: What the early church wrote on each verse, gathered from the Ante-Nicene and Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers.

stance.label: mixed
stance.why: Origen, Didymus the Blind and Evagrius Ponticus Traditional heretical, the rest Neutral.

entries.name: Westminster Confession of Faith
entries.author: Westminster Assembly
